name: Struck Down: Leaders Whose Murders Changed History
description: From Caesar's Ides of March to Benazir Bhutto: twenty centuries of killings of rulers and reformers, and what each one set in motion.

checkpoints.name: Rome's knives
checkpoints.note: Julius Caesar was stabbed by a group of senators in 44 BCE. Later emperors lived under the watch of the Praetorian Guard, whose officers had a hand in several killings: Caligula died in 41, Domitian in 96, Commodus in 192 and Caracalla in 217.

checkpoints.name: A shot that began a war
checkpoints.note: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln in 1865, days after the Civil War's main fighting ended. In 1914 Gavrilo Princip shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, and within weeks Europe was at war in World War I. In January 1919 Rosa Luxemburg was killed in Berlin.

checkpoints.name: Between the wars
checkpoints.note: Michael Collins, an Irish leader, was shot in an ambush in 1922 during the Irish Civil War. Leon Trotsky, exiled by Stalin, was struck with an ice axe in Mexico in 1940 and died the next day. Aung San, who led Burma toward independence, was shot with colleagues in 1947.

checkpoints.name: From Gandhi to King
checkpoints.note: Gandhi was shot in Delhi in January 1948 by a man who opposed his stance toward Muslims. Patrice Lumumba, first prime minister of independent Congo, was killed in 1961. John F. Kennedy was shot in Dallas in 1963, Malcolm X in New York in 1965 and Martin Luther King Jr. in Memphis in 1968.

checkpoints.name: Leaders of South Asia
checkpoints.note: Indira Gandhi, prime minister of India, was shot in 1984 by two of her own bodyguards after an army action at the Golden Temple. In December 2007 Benazir Bhutto, twice prime minister of Pakistan, was killed after an election rally in Rawalpindi.
